authorityBoundary: ADR is not issue status. Issue records are not accepted specs. specs records are not implementation. Nix projection is not SSOT unless bound by projection parity. <feat> provisional findings are evidence only until ADR/specs promotion completes.
consequences: ADR discussion remains required before accepted specs, but implementation findings can be captured as provisional non-authority evidence.
Single-spec issues must be scoped by explicit JSONL records, not by directory proximity or newest-looking files.
Nix deletion cannot happen until JSONL-to-Nix projection parity and omitted-field manifests pass.
The executable bridge belongs in ops as a feat implementation declared by specs.
context: Latest canonical already carries ADR JSONL inputs and issue-ledger-unified-kernel.
Nix definitions can become thinner only after JSONL specs records, projection parity, and omitted-field manifests exist.
Strict ADR-first/specs-first governance can deadlock when implementation discovers a destructive usecase before ADR promotion.
Single-spec issue placement is observable as flat issues/*.jsonl but lacks a canonical issue-to-spec binding record.
decision: Introduce a promotion kernel where ADR raw records provide rationale, specs issue records provide lifecycle, specs record JSONL provides proposed or accepted definitions, Nix acts as deterministic projection adapter, and ops implements the executable audit bridge.

layoutBoundary.src: lib only: core and adapter behavior stays in ops src modules

title: Define ADR to specs issue to specs record promotion and feat implementation start bridge
